trial_court: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Chikkodi, M.C.No.68/2021
case_name: Smt. Anusuya W/O Anand Ghaste vs Shri Anand S/O Khemanna Gaste

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Anusuya W/O Anand Ghaste, wife
parties.respondent_defendant: Shri Anand S/O Khemanna Gaste, husband

facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who got married in 2012. Due to uncordial relationship, they are living separately. The husband filed a divorce petition under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife seeks to withdraw the petition and transfer it to the Principal Judge, Family Court at Hubballi.

legal_principles.principle: The convenience of the wife must be looked into.
legal_principles.held: Usually when a transfer petition is filed by the wife, the convenience of the wife is to be looked into rather than inconvenience that would be caused to the husband.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh Vs. Kumar Sanjay and another (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: At paragraph No.9, which reads as under: '9. The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik (Year) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: The court allows the wife's petition to withdraw the divorce petition and transfer it to the Principal Judge, Family Court at Hubballi.

use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition for a matrimonial case
advising on jurisdictional issues in family courts
assisting with divorce proceedings under Hindu Marriage Act
